correctness.rationale: From first-jet equations u_i u_j=0 and u_i v_j+v_i u_j=0, localizing at P inverts independent v_i and puts z_i=u_i/v_i, yielding z_i+z_j=0, z_i z_j=0 for every edge. Along each connected graph component, path parities force z_i=±t. An odd cycle gives 2t=0 and kills t in odd characteristic; in char2 all signs agree. Each retained component has an edge imposing t²=0, no cross-component constraints, so the local Artin algebra is tensor product of b dual-number factors with squarefree monomial basis length2^b and P minimal. Independently recomputed unsigned incidence nullities and quadratic relations on all 814 graphs on n=2..5 with no isolated vertices across F2,F3,F5 (2442 graph/field instances), matching predicted signless incidence nullity; for a triangle local length is 1 (odd char) vs2 (char2). The structural proof extends beyond finite checks.

value.rationale: Computing generic nilpotent multiplicity of a natural distinguished component in graph-jet schemes directly addresses a published open type of component-invariant problem. The dependence on bipartiteness and field characteristic is a meaningful structural boundary, not a small arbitrary graph census; classifies one component exactly for all graphs in a broad natural class.

final_claim: For the first jet scheme of any finite simple graph edge ideal without isolated vertices, the constant-zero component P=(u_i) has generic local algebra over K=k(v_i) isomorphic to K[ε_1,...,ε_b]/(ε_1²,...,ε_b²), with b equal to the number of bipartite connected components if char(k)≠2, and all connected components if char(k)=2. Its generic multiplicity is 2^b.
limitations: Only finite simple graphs with no isolated vertices and at least one edge; first jets and central zero-constant component only.
No primary decomposition or generic lengths of the other components claimed; residual unindexed equivalence risk.
